findings.title: Update count synchronously after a successful copy.
findings.rationale:
The goroutine writes h.count without h.mu. Concurrent requests cause a data race and lost increments. It also increments the count before ReadFrom confirms that the upload succeeded.

Remove the goroutine. Lock the mutex and increment count after ReadFrom succeeds.

Proposed fix

-	go func() { -		h.count++ -	}() - if _, err := f.ReadFrom(r.Body); err != nil { http.Error(w, fmt.Sprintf("upload failed: %v", err), http.StatusInternalServerError) return }

+	h.mu.Lock() +	h.count++ +	h.mu.Unlock() + w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)

Also applies to: 25-27

findings.title: Set a maximum upload size.
findings.rationale:
The handler copies the complete request body to local storage without a limit. A client can consume all available disk space.

Apply http.MaxBytesReader with a configured upload limit. Return `413 Request Entity Too Large` when the limit is exceeded.

findings.title: Close the file and remove partial uploads on copy failure.
findings.rationale:
f is never closed. Repeated uploads can exhaust file descriptors. If ReadFrom fails after it writes data, the partial file remains at the named destination.

Close the file after creation. Remove the destination file before returning a copy failure.

findings.title: Restrict name to one safe file name.
